items.title: U.S. military reviewing deadly strike on Iranian wedding
items.summary: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) is conducting an internal review of a civilian casualty incident at a wedding during the strikes in Iran last Tuesday, U.S. officials say. The most significant civilian casualty incident happened on the first day of the war when a U.S. strike hit a school, killing 150 people, most of them children. The U.S. military investigation into that incident is expected to be finalized soon, according to a U.S. official. Driving the news: According to the Iranian Red Crescent, a humanitarian network, five people were killed and 67 wounded in the blast that hit the home where the wedding was happening. items.title: Maria Bartiromo fired by Fox
items.summary: Fox News Media fired longtime host Maria Bartiromo for business reasons, a spokesperson confirmed to Axios on Thursday. Why it matters: Bartiromo is considered one of the network's most high profile hosts. The unexpected departure prompted questions about whether she would join the Trump administration. Bartiromo has developed a strong rapport with the president over the last decade. The White House didn't immediately respond to requests for comment. What they're saying: In a statement, Fox News Media said, "We thank Maria for her work over the last 12 ½ years and wish her all the best on her next chapter." Bartiromo was last on air Aug. 9. Editor's note: This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

items.title: Diesel price surges to all-time high, fueled by wars
items.summary: The average price of diesel topped its 2022 record high on Friday , spiking to $5.85 per gallon, per AAA . Why it matters: Farmers, truckers and freight companies have been absorbing higher diesel costs since the Iran war began. The ballooning price threatens to further raise shipping costs while compounding a growing political problem for President Trump . It can also indirectly affect households by putting inflationary pressure on anything Americans buy that's carried by truck, which includes a massive share of goods. Driving the news: Diesel has been rising steadily for weeks, but surged 17 cents in just the last two days. The previous record was $5.816, per AAA, set in June 2022. Diesel typically costs more than gasoline because of higher taxes, stricter environmental regulations requiring expensive refining and a lower production yield per barrel of oil. Worth noting: While the strangling of the Strait of Hormuz cast the global market into disarray, Ukraine's highly effective drone campaign targeting Russian refineries has further strained worldwide diesel refinery capacity. items.title: Historic first: Older adults now outnumber the youngest children for the first time
items.summary: Data: U.S. Census Bureau, International Database ; Chart: Noah Bressner/Axios People 65 and older now outnumber children ages 5 and younger worldwide for the first time in recorded history, according to a new report by the U.S. Census. Why it matters: A global plunge in fertility — demographers' term for the number of children being born — and increased longevity are creating a demographic inversion that's projected to deepen for decades. It's a trend that's shifting the historic balance between working-age people and older adults . By the numbers: The scale and speed of the shift as the youngest Baby Boomers move toward their mid-60s are striking. They reflect the scope of the challenge in caring for the elderly and maintaining programs such as Social Security in the U.S., an Axios analysis of the Census data found. More than 71% of the world's population lived in countries with fertility rates at or below the roughly 2.1-births-per-woman replacement level in 2023. That's up from 45% in 2013. items.title: Gloria Steinem, feminist icon, dies at 92
items.summary: Gloria Steinem, the journalist, activist and organizer who became the most recognizable face of the U.S. women's movement, died Wednesday at 92. The big picture: Steinem resisted being cast as feminism's singular face, but for six decades she carried its ideas into mainstream America across its second and third waves. Steinem made the personal political: An illegal abortion at 22 preceded decades of fighting first to legalize abortion and then to defend that right. Steinem died peacefully, surrounded by people who loved her at her home in New York City, according to a Thursday announcement posted from her and her foundation's Instagram accounts. "Gloria's greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard," the announcement said. Flashback: Steinem first drew national attention as a journalist in 1963 when she went undercover as a Playboy Bunny and exposed the job's low pay and sexist treatment. Soon, she was both chronicling feminism's emerging second wave and organizing within it. items.summary: TLDR: Psychology, economics, and other disciplines describe agents as systems driven by beliefs and desires. This post argues that the belief-desire view can be derived from classic theorems from optimal control and reinforcement learning. This suggests seeing beliefs and desires as properties of optimal policies rather than as assumptions from folk psychology. Introduction One way to think about agents is as "systems that act for reasons". items.title: “What is neuralese and why is it bad?” by Linch
items.summary: What is neuralese? To explain neuralese, we need to first understand chain-of-thought, one of the largest developments in AI in the last five years. Right now AIs think broadly but shallowly in a single forward pass. The model gives you an immediate snap answer to a question you might be interested in. They can be pretty smart in their snap answers,, but mostly they can’t do very advanced reasoning tasks like complicated math or programming: .The solution that the frontier AI companies have come up with is called chain-of-thought. Basically the model runs one forward pass, writes down some intermediate thoughts in natural language in a journal, and then that's fed back into the model to run another pass. This loop is repeated until the model is somewhat confident it has the right answer (or it hits a cap on thinking time), and then it outputs the user-visible results (for example a chatbot's response to your question, or working code). The looping step is often called “recurrence.” Natural-language chain-of-thought is a major advance in letting models reason for longer, but it also has an accidental safety benefit.
